issue.title: Bug: MP3 files with embedded album art fail during processing

nextActions: Review the reported behavior and build instructions; define the baseline failure before cloning or scheduling a build.
limitations: READY_TO_INVESTIGATE means metadata is sufficient to begin engineering review, not a reproduced or repaired bug.
Dependency manifests are scanned heuristically; transitive dependencies, availability of registry packages, native libraries and physical equipment are not verified.
Explicit PR references and explicit first-person work claims are matched; semantically related work, off-platform coordination and unusual wording can be missed.
Runtime compatibility, contribution policy and complete reproduction steps still require engineering review.

dimensions.reason: Valid Pro Tools MP3 exports fail solely because they contain album art.
The report and collaborator follow-up were posted within the last day.
The project collaborator supplied a reproduction comparison and a concrete FFmpeg observation.
Attached artwork must not classify an audio file as video, and audio outputs must select the audio stream.
A generated MP3 with attached_pic deterministically entered the video branch and failed preview conversion.
evidence: local red fixture run with FFmpeg 9.0.1

dimensions.reason: The repair changes three FFmpeg stream-selection arguments in one module.
Generated fixtures cover plain MP3, covered MP3, and actual video without hardware.
Real video detection remains enabled while audio conversion explicitly chooses the first audio stream.
The repository has current commits and an active collaborator response.
Embedded artwork is common in MP3 files uploaded for transcription.
The selection applies to any audio input with attached artwork or unrelated non-audio streams.
Correct classification restores both transcription WAV creation and the audio preview path.

ranking.deliveryNote: Readiness is an evidence-based human assessment, not a calibrated probability. Unknown inputs are never scored as facts.
